title: Console: Scaling audit trail for Dedicated autoscaling (events, filters, retention, “why did we scale?”)
creator: Chloe Martin
project: Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Goal
Expose autoscaling decision events for Dedicated pools in Redwood Console with enough context to answer:
- What changed (desired vs applied replicas)?
- Was the decision clamped to min/max bounds?
- Why did we scale (top contributing signals + cooldown/guardrails)?
- When/where did it happen (region/hardware class)?

Background
With min/max bounds (ENG-2841/2843) and new decision metrics (ENG-2846), customers expect strict spend control and transparency. Support tickets (e.g., SUP-4821, SUP-4874) indicate we need an audit trail to build trust and reduce escalations.

User stories
1) Dedicated admin: “Show me a history of scaling actions for pool X over the last 24h; I need to correlate latency spikes with scaling.”
2) FinOps / eng lead: “Confirm we never scaled above max; if we did, I need evidence and a postmortem path.”
3) Oncall / TAM: “Explain throttling when customer set max too low; point to specific clamp events and the reason.”

Scope (this ticket)
Backend
- Add Console API endpoints to query scaling decision/audit events for a Dedicated pool.
- Implement pagination + time range filtering.
- Enforce RBAC: only users with access to the owning org/project + Dedicated pool can view events.
- Retention policy enforcement in the query layer (do not surface older-than-retention records).

UI
- Add a “Scaling History” panel on Dedicated Pool details.
- Filters: time range (preset + custom), event type, clamp reason, region.
- Detail drawer: “Why did we scale?” explanation that is deterministic and derived from structured event fields.

Non-goals
- Customer-config change audit history (who changed min/max). That’s a separate Console + control-plane audit log effort.
- Export to customer SIEM / webhook delivery.
- Per-request / per-route traces of autoscaling decisions.

Event schema (consumer contract)
We consume structured decision logs emitted by autoscaler (ENG-2843/ENG-2846). Console will treat these fields as the stable UI contract:
- event_time
- pool_id
- region
- hardware_class
- previous_replicas
- desired_replicas (pre-clamp)
- applied_replicas (post-clamp)
- min_replicas / max_replicas (evaluated)
- action: scale_up | scale_down | no_op
- clamp_reason: none | max_bound | min_bound | cooldown | rate_limit | capacity_shortage | freeze
- top_signals (bounded list, max 3): queue_depth, gpu_util, p95_latency, throttles, forecast_qps, forecast_confidence
- cooldown_remaining_s
- decision_id (for support correlation)

“Why did we scale?” rules (v1)
Render a single sentence summary + bullet details using the following precedence:
- If clamp_reason != none: start with clamp summary (e.g., “Desired 10 replicas but clamped to max=8.”)
- Then include the strongest signal summary from top_signals (queue/util/latency/forecast).
- Include guardrail context if present (cooldown/rate_limit/freeze/capacity_shortage).
- Avoid raw metric dumps; keep deterministic formatting.

Retention
- GA default: 30 days of scaling events visible in Console.
- Internally allow a config knob for longer retention for enterprise add-ons, but UI copy should reflect the org’s configured retention if available; otherwise “30 days”.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Pool details page shows Scaling History for allowlisted orgs.
- [x] Filtering works (time range, type, clamp reason, region).
- [x] Detail view includes “why” explanation and raw fields for support copy/paste (decision_id, desired/applied, bounds).
- [x] Events older than retention are not shown.
- [x] RBAC tested: user without pool access gets 403.
- [x] Performance: p95 < 600ms for 24h query for typical pools (<= 5k events/day).
- [x] No high-cardinality labels exposed in UI filters (avoid “model”, “route”, “customer_request_id”).

References
- PRD: confluence/product-docs/requirements/autoscaling-bounds-predictive-prd.json
- Design spec: confluence/product-docs/design-specs/dedicated-autoscaling-bounds-design-spec.json (Console section)
- Runbook context: confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/runbook-dedicated-autoscaling-anomalies.json
- Support pain: SUP-4821 (spend exceeded), SUP-4874 (max too low -> throttling)

Implementation links

- UI PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-22011.json
comments: 2026-01-16 (Chloe Martin): Creating ticket based on Dedicated bounds launch requirements. Key requirement from CS: reduce “why did we scale?” back-and-forth; must be explainable and bounded. Assigning Felix for UI implementation; I’ll coordinate backend endpoints + RBAC review with Jada.

2026-01-18 (Alicia Perez): UX note: keep the default view lightweight. Proposed layout: table with time, action (up/down/no-op), applied replicas (X→Y), clamp badge, and a short “why” snippet. Details panel expands for signal breakdown. Avoid exposing raw utilization numbers unless in details.

2026-01-22 (Jada Williams): Backend approach: query from observability event store (same source as scaling decision metrics) via console backend. Must enforce org+pool scoping at query time (don’t rely on front-end filtering). Add cursor pagination, max 500 records/page, server-side time bounds required.

2026-01-24 (Allison Grant): Please ensure the explanation string is deterministic and derived from event fields only (no additional joins). We should not accidentally leak other pools’ info via aggregation. Also: include decision_id and clamp_reason explicitly for oncall correlation with runbook.

2026-02-01 (Marcus Lin): Security/RBAC review: ok to display scaling events; contains operational metadata only. Ensure no customer prompt payloads / request IDs. Confirm retention text is accurate per org configuration; if unknown, say “up to 30 days” rather than a hard guarantee.

2026-02-05 (Felix Schneider): Backend endpoint available in PR-22003 with RBAC checks. Added 403 tests + pagination tests. UI hooked up in PR-22011. Added copy: “Scaling events retained for ~30 days” (pending final retention config source).

2026-02-07 (Rafael Mendes): Oncall usability: please add a direct link from the detail drawer to the runbook section “Interpreting clamp_reason”. Also add a one-liner warning when clamp_reason=max_bound that customer may see throttling if demand exceeds max.

2026-02-10 (Felix Schneider): Incorporated runbook link + warning callout. Added deterministic “Why did we scale?” sentence builder: clamp summary first, then top signal, then guardrail context.
